item.title: Lawyer Tony Buzbee must face $25 million defamation lawsuit, judge says
item.description: Prominent Texas lawyer Tony Buzbee has failed for now to defeat a $25 million defamation lawsuit brought against him by a Mississippi attorney he accused of soliciting his former clients to bring lawsuits against him.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: Prominent Texas lawyer Tony Buzbee has failed for now to defeat a $25 million defamation lawsuit brought against him by a Mississippi attorney he accused of soliciting his former clients to bring lawsuits against him. US District Judge Vincent Brown in Galveston, Texas, ruled that Buzbee and his law firm must face the lawsuit from Marcy Croft, which grew out of litigation involving rapper Shawn "Jay-Z" Carter. The judge denied a motion to dismiss the case, ruling that the court at this early stage of the case could "reasonably infer" that Buzbee made defamatory statements about Croft, who has represented Carter's entertainment company Roc Nation. Buzbee said in an email that Croft's lawsuit is a "completely frivolous case and it will massively backfire on her." Gregg Costa, a lawyer at Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher representing Croft, said in a statement that they looked forward to "holding the defendants accountable for the reputational damage they caused to a distinguished and honorable lawyer." The ruling marks the latest development in a multi-front legal battle spanning nearly two years. At its core was a lawsuit brought by Buzbee against Carter in Manhattan federal court on behalf of an anonymous plaintiff who claimed she was drugged and raped by Carter and Sean "Diddy" Combs when she was 13 at an afterparty for the 2000 MTV Music Awards. Carter and Combs denied the allegations, which the plaintiff later withdrew. That lawsuit spawned other litigation from Carter against Buzbee in California state court, as well as a case Buzbee brought against Croft, Roc Nation and Carter's lawyers at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan in Texas, alleging that Croft used agents who solicited his former clients in order to bring claims against him. Both cases were dismissed. Croft's defamation lawsuit in Texas cites social media posts by Buzbee and says his claims of illegal client solicitation were part of a "coordinated campaign to falsely accuse a well-respected attorney of criminal conduct." The lawsuit seeks at least $25 million in damages. Carter has also sued Buzbee for defamation and malicious prosecution in New York federal court, after Buzbee's client [USN:L1N3P518Y TEXT:"dropped her lawsuit"] against the music stars last year. In that case, Carter claims Buzbee pursued rape allegations he knew to be false in the hopes of securing a payout. Buzbee, in court papers filed last month, countered that Carter was using the court system to harass both the alleged victim and her lawyers. Last week, Buzbee's former client [USN:L6N45H0YJ TEXT:"recanted her claim of rape"] against Carter and said she never met the billionaire rapper. She said she did not review the lawsuit against Carter before it was filed. Buzbee has asked a Manhattan federal judge to strike his former client's declaration . "Everything that is being said by Carter's team is a lie and it will be proven to be a lie with documents and audio, and even video," Buzbee told Reuters. Carter's lawyers did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In court papers filed on Monday , Carter said Buzbee and his firm "exploited Doe to pursue their own financial interests without investigating her claims and mental health issues."

item.title: Procurador da Califórnia intima OpenAI sobre riscos da IA
item.description: O procurador-geral do estado norte-americano da Califórnia, Rob Bonta, emitiu uma intimação investigativa à OpenAI, como parte de um inquérito mais amplo sobre incidentes e riscos de segurança digital relacionados aos modelos de inteligência artificial da companhia, informou seu gabinete nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O procurador-geral do estado norte-americano da Califórnia, Rob Bonta, emitiu uma intimação investigativa à OpenAI, como parte de um inquérito mais amplo sobre incidentes e riscos de segurança digital relacionados aos modelos de inteligência artificial da companhia, informou seu gabinete nesta quinta-feira. No mês passado, Bonta anunciou que o Departamento de Justiça dos Estados Unidos estava conduzindo uma investigação formal sobre o “incidente Hugging Face”. Agentes de IA desenvolvidos pela OpenAI invadiram sistemas da Hugging Face no início deste ano, obtendo acesso a partes da infraestrutura da plataforma de código aberto e expondo os riscos de segurança eletrônica associados a sistemas de IA cada vez mais avançados. “Meu gabinete está fazendo perguntas adicionais à OpenAI sobre incidentes e riscos de segurança cibernética envolvendo a empresa e seus modelos de IA”, disse Bonta em comunicado. Ele alertou que os desenvolvedores que não garantirem que seus modelos de IA não cometam ou possibilitem ataques digitais poderão enfrentar responsabilização legal. A OpenAI não comentou o assunto. A Comissão Federal de Comércio dos EUA (FTC) também está conduzindo uma investigação em todo o setor envolvendo Anthropic, OpenAI e outras empresas de IA para revelar os perigos potenciais que sua tecnologia representa para os consumidores, informou uma autoridade sênior da FTC à Reuters na quarta-feira. A investigação é a primeira ação oficial de fiscalização dos EUA que se aprofunda sobre agentes de IA. A procuradora-geral do estado norte-americano de Iowa, Brenna Bird, lidera uma coalizão de procuradores-gerais de 15 estados dos EUA, incluindo Alabama, Arkansas, Texas e Utah, na busca por informações da OpenAI sobre o ataque à Hugging Face, que a Nvidia fez acordo em setembro para comprar por US$12,93 bilhões. OpenAI e Anthropic estão investigando inúmeros casos em que seus agentes de IA invadiram sistemas comerciais e governamentais. (Por Jaspreet Singh)

item.title: Ireland v Austria game briefly halted by Stop the Game protesters
item.description: Thursday's Nations League Group B3 match between Ireland and Austria was disrupted when tennis balls were thrown onto the pitch at the Aviva Stadium by those protesting against the Irish team fulfilling their fixtures against Israel.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thursday's Nations League Group B3 match between Ireland and Austria was disrupted when tennis balls were thrown onto the pitch at the Aviva Stadium by those protesting against the Irish team fulfilling their fixtures against Israel. Ireland were 1-0 up in front of a sell-out crowd when the referee suspended the match briefly in the 20th minute as tennis balls featuring the Palestinian flag were thrown onto the pitch. Ireland are one of Europe's most outspoken critics of Israel's war in Gaza , and protests calling for the team to boycott the fixtures with Israel have been ongoing since February's Nations League draw pitted the two countries together. Ireland keeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad on the eve of Sunday's 3-0 away win over Israel, played in Hungary, which went ahead after the players held two votes on Saturday, with a majority opting to fulfil the fixture. Bazunu is back in the squad and on the bench for Thursday's game with Austria but will not take part in the home game against Israel, scheduled for next Sunday, which was moved by the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) to Serbia and will be played behind closed doors in Backa Topola. Troy Parrott put Ireland ahead in the 12th minute, dancing through the Austrian defence and into the area before striking low into the far corner. FAI members [USN:L8N3WJ27T TEXT:"voted in November"] for its board to request that UEFA suspend Israel from European competitions, but a motion in favour of proceeding with the fixtures was passed at a meeting in July.

item.title: Boeing white-collar workers approve latest contract offer, averting strike fears
item.description: Boeing's largest white-collar union said on Thursday its members approved a sweetened contract offer, easing fears of a strike that could have stalled work on two long-delayed jetliners and slowed the pace of aircraft deliveries.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Boeing's (BA.N) largest white-collar union said on Thursday its members approved a sweetened contract offer, easing fears of a strike that could have stalled work on two long-delayed jetliners and slowed the pace of aircraft deliveries. The Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace, which represents about 17,000 Boeing workers, said both its bargaining units voted to approve the new four-year offer. The [USN:L6N45317M TEXT:"proposal"] included a guaranteed 10% wage increase upon ratification, along with annual raises of 4% and the possibility of an additional 2% hike based on performance. About 68% of the professional unit, which represents roughly 13,000 engineers and scientists, voted in favor of the deal, as did over 53% of the technical unit, representing about 4,000 designers, analysts and technicians. The two units bargain together but vote separately. The ratification provides much-needed relief for Boeing, easing concerns over a potential strike as early as October 7, the day after current contracts expire. A work stoppage could have delayed critical certification efforts for the 737 MAX 10 narrowbody and 777X widebody, while also disrupting the company's plans to increase production and accelerate deliveries. Members of both the professional and technical units had previously [USN:L6N44I12F TEXT:"rejected"] Boeing's initial offer, which linked guaranteed raises to inflation, capped at 3%, with up to an additional 2.5% based on performance. SPEEA's last strike against Boeing was in 2000, when engineers and technical workers walked out for 40 days in a dispute over pay and benefits. The stoppage, which affected commercial-aircraft production and deliveries, was one of the largest white-collar strikes in US history.

item.title: YPF investors ask U.S. Supreme Court to revive $16.1 billion judgment against Argentina
item.description: Investment firms Petersen Energia and Eton Park petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court on Wednesday to reinstate a $16.1 billion judgment against Argentina in the long-running YPF litigation.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Siniawski, Leila Miller
item.content:encoded: Investment firms Petersen Energia and Eton Park petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court on Wednesday to reinstate a $16.1 billion judgment against Argentina in the long-running YPF litigation. The petition seeks to [USN:L6N40F0U2 TEXT:"overturn a March decision"] by the 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, which held the claims belonged in Argentine courts rather than the United States. That decision overturned a judgment entered after more than a decade of litigation. The investors argue the ruling improperly allows a foreign nation to rely on its own laws to avoid liability in U.S. courts. BACKGROUND The dispute centers on Argentina's 2012 [USN:BRE84306W TEXT:"nationalization of a controlling stake"] in YPF. Petersen and Eton Park allege Argentina violated YPF's bylaws by failing to launch a tender offer to minority shareholders after seizing a 51% stake from Spain's Repsol. Argentina amended YPF's bylaws prior to its 1993 New York Stock Exchange listing to require a mandatory tender offer to all shareholders if the government ever regained majority control. A U.S. district court had previously entered a $16.1 billion judgment — described in the petition as the largest commercial award in U.S. history — after a three-day damages trial. KEY ARGUMENTS The petition asks whether a foreign sovereign can use its own law to require claims to be brought to its domestic courts despite jurisdiction established under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act. It also questions whether U.S. courts should defer to a sovereign's interpretation of its own law when that interpretation is first advanced on appeal. The petition, filed by former U.S. Solicitor General Paul Clement, argues the 2nd Circuit decision conflicts with Supreme Court precedent and creates a split among federal appellate courts. Argentina's presidential office did not immediately respond to requests for comment. YPF declined to comment.

item.title: UMG sued by Bill Withers' publisher over Olivia Dean song
item.description: The music publisher for late R&B great Bill Withers sued Universal Music Group on Thursday, alleging that an Olivia Dean song from her hit album "The Art of Loving" unlawfully copied Withers' classic "Just the Two of Us."
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: The music publisher for late R&B great Bill Withers sued Universal Music Group (UMG.AS) on Thursday, alleging that an Olivia Dean song from her hit album "The Art of Loving" unlawfully copied Withers' classic "Just the Two of Us." Bleunig Music said in the complaint that Dean's "I've Seen It" lifted elements from "Just the Two of Us" including the "distinctively protectable melody" of Withers' song Spokespeople for UMG did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the complaint Dean herself is not a defendant in the lawsuit Bleunig said that Withers was under contract with the company when he co-wrote "Just the Two of Us," which peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart in 1981 "I've Seen It" is the closing song on Dean's breakthrough 2025 album "The Art of Loving," which has been certified gold in the United States by the Recording Industry Association of America Dean won the Grammy Award for Best New Artist earlier this year The case is Bleunig Music v. Capitol Records LLC, US District Court for the Central District of California, No. 2:26-cv-11383. For Bleunig: Clair Burrill For UMG: attorney information not yet available

item.title: Colonos israelíes matan a un palestino en Cisjordania, según fuentes oficiales
item.description: Colonos israelíes dispararon el jueves contra dos palestinos y uno de ellos murió mientras que el otro resultó herido, en un ataque contra la localidad de Yasuf, en Cisjordania, ocupada por Israel, según fuentes oficiales palestinas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colonos israelíes dispararon el jueves contra dos palestinos y uno de ellos murió mientras que el otro resultó herido, en un ataque contra la localidad de Yasuf, en Cisjordania, ocupada por Israel, según fuentes oficiales palestinas. En una oleada de violencia, el ejército israelí y los colonos han matado a más de 80 palestinos en Cisjordania desde principios de 2026, según la ONU. En el último incidente, los colonos mataron a tiros a Mashour Yassin, de 51 años, durante un ataque a su casa en las afueras de Yasuf, según declaró el presidente del consejo municipal, Jumaa Abdel Fattah. Los agresores llegaron desde un puesto avanzado de colonos construido cerca de la localidad hace unos dos meses, explicó Fattah. "Los colonos llevan atacando la localidad de forma continuada desde que se estableció el asentamiento", añadió. El ejército israelí afirmó que los palestinos habían lanzado piedras contra los israelíes que se acercaban al pueblo, y que las fuerzas armadas dispersaron a los implicados. Añadió que el ejército israelí había disparado contra los palestinos. No aclaró de inmediato por qué los colonos israelíes estaban invadiendo el pueblo. Fattah afirmó que los colonos habían disparado a los dos palestinos antes de que llegara el ejército israelí. El ejército israelí no hizo comentarios inmediatos sobre el momento en que se produjeron los hechos. Organizaciones de derechos humanos afirman que la creciente presencia de colonos en las afueras de las aldeas forma parte de una campaña para apropiarse de tierras y mermar el territorio en el que los palestinos pretenden establecer un Estado. Israel ocupó Cisjordania en 1967 y, desde entonces, el territorio ha estado bajo ocupación militar israelí, con los colonos envalentonados por el Gobierno del primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu, quien ha supervisado una expansión masiva de los asentamientos judíos. La ONU y la mayoría de los países consideran que los asentamientos israelíes son ilegales según el derecho internacional que regula las ocupaciones militares. Israel no está de acuerdo con esa interpretación y afirma que el estatus del territorio es objeto de controversia.

item.title: Global M&A deal rush fades in third quarter as rising borrowing costs bite
item.description: M&A activity in the last three months totalled $993 billion, down 41% compared to the second quarter of 2026, marking the first quarter to fall below $1 trillion since the second quarter of 2025, according to LSEG data.
item.dc:creator: Anousha Sakoui, Echo Wang
item.content:encoded: M&A activity in the last three months totalled $993 billion, down 41% compared to the second quarter of 2026, marking the first quarter to fall below $1 trillion since the second quarter of 2025, according to LSEG data. Banca Monte dei Paschi's [USN:L8N45607I TEXT:"$32 billion bid"] for Banco BPM (BAMI.MI) and Gold Fields (GFIJ.J) $25.7 billion [USN:L1N45K003 TEXT:"bid"] for Northern Star Resources (NST.AX) were among the 10 deals over $10 billion announced in the third quarter, the lowest number of quarterly megadeals since the fourth quarter of 2024. While the boom in artificial intelligence and data centre building has lifted the outlook for economic growth, surging energy costs have been fanning inflation and pushing expectations higher about where interest rates will settle. The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield hit [USN:L6N4570XY TEXT:"5.34"]% on Thursday, its highest level since 2002, after posting the biggest quarterly rise this century in the three months to September. "At the margins [higher yields] makes valuations sometimes a little tougher," said John Collins, global head of M&A at Morgan Stanley. "That said, the impact is hard to quantify, so I'm not ready to call a slowdown based on what we are seeing." So far this year worldwide M&A is up 28% to $3.9 trillion, the highest level in the period since 2001, while the number of deals fell 8%, levels not seen since 2020. “Corporates are still looking for scale or access to markets and technologies they are not in," said Carsten Woehrn, Goldman Sachs' co-head of M&A in Europe, Middle East and Africa. He sees total deal value exceeding the 2021 peak if the pace continues. "Megadeals are continuing and we’ve seen significant activity since the summer," Woehrn said. "Boards feel a greater urgency to pull the trigger on strategic deals.” Historic levels of investment in the technology sector have bolstered deals, with strategic stake purchases in those companies accounting for about one quarter of global M&A so far this year. Earlier this year, both Claude maker Anthropic and ChatGPT maker OpenAI raised tens of billions of US dollars from investors. While US and European dealmaking fell sharply in the last three months, Asia Pacific M&A totalled $242 billion, up 8% from the second quarter and up 36% from the same period last year. This has been the strongest year to date for global private equity-backed dealmaking by value since records began in 1980, but the third quarter also saw a slowdown versus the same period last year. Cross-border dealmaking remains a strong theme this year to date, up 32% on the same period last year. "We're seeing a fair amount of appetite from US companies thinking about acquisitions in Europe for the first time, taking advantage of a strong dollar. In reverse, you're seeing people considering investment in the U.S. to take advantage of the potentially higher growth opportunity in the country," said Charlie Bouckaert, JPMorgan’s global head of M&A. TRILLION DOLLAR IPOs AND DEALMAKING New listings, particularly in the technology sector, have fuelled M&A giving the companies new currency to buy up rivals. SpaceX [USN:L4N42O0VX TEXT:"acquired"] AI coding startup Cursor just days after its blockbuster Nasdaq debut, which saw its valuation surge to more than $2 trillion. "One of the drivers of activity is that being larger may help companies navigate transition in AI better," Collins said. The June IPO of Elon Musk's SpaceX (SPCX.O) helped drive $215 billion worth of initial public offerings, excluding SPACs, priced globally in the year to date, the highest level since 2021, from a lower number of deals than in the same period last year. In the last three months, stock sales raised US$284 billion, 26% less than the proceeds raised across equity capital markets during the second quarter, though marking a 39% increase from third quarter of 2025, thanks to offerings from SK Hynix (000660.KS) and Intel (INTC.O) . Some bankers did sound a note of caution however that some investors were taking more of a pause when approaching some technology and AI-related deals. "Until about 10 days ago, no one seemed to worry about the midterms, but with rising diesel prices and rates and a risk of a change in political direction, it is prompting caution, ” said Andreas Bernstorff, global head of equity capital markets at BNP Paribas. In recent weeks some IPOs have been delayed as higher interest rates and setbacks in the data center ecosystem [USN:L6N45H0SG TEXT:"threaten to derail"] a slew of new issues from the sector. Even with the uncertainty ahead, bankers remain confident. “Strong secular trends (such as AI) are driving activity, and we expect 2027 to be another robust year,” Bouckaert said.

item.title: Republicans’ awkward midterms dance with Trump
item.description: US President Donald Trump is trying out a new pitch ahead of what’s expected to be a hectic 32 days of travel as Republicans confront voters’ unhappiness with an unpopular president. If only, Trump laments, the American people knew just how well the country was doing.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump is trying out a new pitch ahead of what’s expected to be a [USN:L1N45L12S TEXT:"hectic 32 days of travel"] as Republicans confront voters’ unhappiness with an unpopular president. If only, [USN:L1N45M10K TEXT:"Trump laments"], the American people knew just how well the country was doing. “We’re doing an extremely poor job of promotion and an extremely great job of running the country,” he told a White House gathering on Wednesday. He posted similar sentiments on Truth Social twice more during the week. The best person to carry that message, he has decided, is Trump himself. “I thought I was finished campaigning,” he joked to the crowd in the East Room of the White House. Republicans are fanning out across battleground states armed with promises on utility bills, manufacturing jobs and economic growth. But this close to Election Day, and with [USN:L6N45G0RV TEXT:"seemingly winnable races slipping further to the left"], are voters still listening? While the nation is near full employment and economic growth is strong, opinion polls show that Americans are struggling with the high cost of living and growing weary of the war against Iran, which has driven energy prices up and further squeezed household budgets. At the same time, Republicans are losing support in key constituencies of the coalition that returned Trump to the White House. Republicans return to voters with few major legislative accomplishments to celebrate, though tax cuts on tips, overtime and some Social Security benefits led to larger tax refunds for many Americans this year. Senate Republicans sought for weeks to pass legislation aimed at preventing [USN:S0N43U01R TEXT:"AI data center construction"] from driving up household electricity bills, but the measure stalled, joining a string of election-year proposals derailed by Democratic opposition and Republican divisions. The White House spent this week touting new initiatives in states where Republicans now face unexpectedly competitive races. Trump unveiled a new steel mill project in [USN:L6N45F193 TEXT:"Iowa"] and [USN:L1N45M0IK TEXT:"plans for an Alaska fossil fuel pipeline."] He’s off to Oklahoma and Alabama on Thursday and Friday, using rallies in safe Republican states to boost campaigns nationwide and reach voters in nearby competitive regions through local media coverage. But some Republican candidates and voters are breaking with Trump on some of his signature issues that have proven politically contentious, including the Iran war, data centers, and the crackdown on illegal migration. Trump, whose administration is running government-funded Trump-centric ads appealing to Americans to “love me,” appeared to acknowledge the challenge on Wednesday, urging voters to look past their feelings about him and focus instead on the Republican agenda. “Even if you don’t like somebody so much, it doesn’t matter. It’s a vote for good things,” he said, encouraging supporters once again to pretend that he is on the ballot. Answer by Joseph Ax Nine states have new US House maps in place after the redistricting war that unfolded over the last year. Republicans were the clear winners: the party gained an advantage in 15 districts across those states, while Democrats improved their chances in only six districts. However, Democrats remain favored to win the House, with Trump’s weak approval ratings dragging down his party’s candidates. There are about 40 seats in play in November out of 435 nationwide, meaning that a small fraction of voters will likely determine which party controls the House. While some of the maps still face legal challenges, none of the litigation appears likely to alter any district lines ahead of November’s election. The Trump administration has told Germany and France to draw down emergency diesel inventories to help to ease global fuel prices or face a potential US diesel export ban, Reuters reported earlier on Thursday. item.title: Canada is not close to restoring housing affordability, says central bank
item.description: By Promit Mukherjee
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: By Promit Mukherjee OTTAWA, Oct 1 (Reuters) - Canada is on the right track to addressing the issue of housing affordability but still has a way to go and needs more time, senior Bank of Canada deputy governor Carolyn Rogers said on Thursday. Restoring affordability will require more supply, better planning and infrastructure, regulations that protect resilience, and incentives that do not add demand to a market already short on supply, she told a business audience in Victoria, British Columbia. Here are the highlights of her speech: * As house prices go up they push rents higher as well as limit people's ability to buy, but at the same time if prices fall it shrinks the overall household wealth. "It feels a bit like a trap," she said. * The affordability goal has to be a mix of policy which could increase supply, protect resilience and reduce the economy's dependence on rising house prices. * "We're on the right track on many of these things, but we have a way to go and it will take time," she said. * Monetary policy can influence demand across the economy, including demand for housing, but it is too blunt a tool to deal with affordability issues * There are no simple fixes to the monetary policy framework that can help * The BoC needs to explain these trade-offs better and be clear with Canadians about what monetary policy can and cannot do, she said. (Reporting by Promit Mukherjee, editing by David Ljunggren) ((Reuters Ottawa editorial; david.ljunggren@tr.com )) Keywords: CANADA CENBANK/

item.title: Dream F Angel Reese named Defensive Player of the Year
item.description: Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese was named the 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese was named the 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year on Thursday. Reese, 24, received 46 votes from a national panel of 74 sportswriters and broadcasters after setting league records for total rebounds (521) and double-doubles (32). Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams finished second with 20 votes, followed by Las Vegas Aces center-forward A'ja Wilson with four votes. Reese averaged a career-high 16.4 points and a league-high 12.1 rebounds in 43 games during her third season in the WNBA and first in Atlanta. The three-time All-Star finished third in the league in both steals per game (1.8) and total thefts (77) and set a career high with 32 blocked shots. Behind Reese, Atlanta ranked third in the WNBA in defensive rating (103.5). Her rebounding helped the Dream allow a league-low 9.5 second-chance points per game. Acquired from the Chicago Sky in a preseason trade on April 6, Reese is the first player in Dream history to win Defensive Player of the Year honors. --Field Level Media

item.title: Vídeo de Xuxa contra Bolsonaro é editado para simular críticas a Lula
item.description: Um vídeo em que a apresentadora Xuxa critica "falas horríveis" do "nosso presidente" e pede que "não votem nesse homem" é de 2022 e se referia ao ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, mas posts nas redes sociais espalham uma versão editada para simular que ela falava recentemente sobre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo em que a apresentadora Xuxa critica "falas horríveis" do "nosso presidente" e pede que "não votem nesse homem" é de 2022 e se referia ao ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, mas posts nas redes sociais espalham uma versão editada para simular que ela falava recentemente sobre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. "Gente! Veja só o que a Xuxa falou sobre o Lula: 'Não vote nesse homem", diz a legenda de uma postagem no Instagram . Xuxa publicou o vídeo original no seu perfil no Instagram em 19 de outubro de 2022, criticando uma entrevista de Bolsonaro em que ele usou a expressão " pintou um clima " ao falar sobre meninas venezuelanas. Na época, Bolsonaro gravou um vídeo dizendo que suas palavras foram distorcidas e que refletiam sua preocupação "no sentido de evitar qualquer tipo de exploração". A assessoria de Xuxa encaminhou à Reuters uma postagem em que a apresentadora afirma que não gravou nenhum vídeo para a atual eleição. Até esta quinta-feira, não havia publicações nas redes sociais dela pedindo que eleitores não votem em Lula. FALAS DE LULA O vídeo checado intercala trechos da fala de Xuxa com um discurso de Lula em Belém, na última segunda-feira, dizendo que mulheres "aprendem a tomar toque desde pequenas" ao mencionar a resistência de homens ao exame de próstata. No dia seguinte, em Salvador, Lula acusou adversários de distorcerem sua fala, como se estivesse normalizando casos de abuso infantil, e disse que estava comparando a coragem de homens e mulheres para fazerem exames médicos. O conteúdo também mostra um trecho de um discurso de Lula na entrega de unidades habitacionais em Recife, em julho de 2024, dizendo que um dos beneficiados “se casou com uma menina que tinha 12 anos”. A oposição criticou a fala de Lula na época. VEREDICTO Falso. Xuxa fazia críticas a Bolsonaro no vídeo original, após uma fala sobre meninas venezuelanas, e não a Lula depois de um discurso sobre exames de toque. item.title: SoftBank completes final phase of $30 billion investment in OpenAI
item.description: SoftBank Group said on Thursday it has completed its $30 billion investment in OpenAI as part of its commitment to the ChatGPT maker's last fundraising round.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: SoftBank Group (9984.T) said on Thursday it has completed its $30 billion investment in OpenAI as part of its commitment to the ChatGPT maker's last fundraising round. Here are some other details: Earlier this year, OpenAI had secured $122 billion in commitments that valued the Sam Altman-led company at $852 billion. Amazon (AMZN.O) , Nvidia (NVDA.O) and SoftBank had anchored the fundraising. The Japanese investment conglomerate, led by founder Masayoshi Son, previously agreed to invest the capital through three tranches of $10 billion each through its Vision Fund 2. SoftBank [USN:L6N45F1AU TEXT:"raised $11.1 billion"] last month in the largest high-yield corporate bond sale globally to fund its mammoth bet on OpenAI. It has become one of the world's biggest backers of OpenAI under founder [USN:L6N45G0LE TEXT:"Son's push"] to make the Japanese conglomerate a dominant investor in AI. SoftBank's cumulative investment in OpenAI stands at $64.6 billion, giving it a 13% stake in the AI lab. It has canceled the remaining $10 billion of undrawn capacity under its [USN:L4N40F0O3 TEXT:"$40 billion bridge loan"] secured earlier this year.

item.title: CAF aprueba paquete de 3.500 millones de dólares para 10 países de América Latina
item.description: El Banco de Desarrollo de América Latina y el Caribe (CAF) aprobó un paquete de 3.500 millones de dólares para 10 países de América Latina, informó el jueves organismo multilateral en un comunicado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Banco de Desarrollo de América Latina y el Caribe (CAF) aprobó un paquete de 3.500 millones de dólares para 10 países de América Latina, informó el jueves organismo multilateral en un comunicado. Los recursos serán destinados a impulsar infraestructura, movilidad sostenible, transición energética, acción climática, educación, recuperación ante desastres y desarrollo productivo, precisó la entidad. Del total de recursos, 1.250 millones de dólares fueron aprobados para Colombia y se enfocarán en la reconstrucción tras el terremoto del 10 de agosto, en proyectos de acción climática y economía azul, el corredor férreo La Dorada–Chiriguaná, el Plan de Desarrollo de Medellín y de Inversiones del Metro de esa ciudad. Otros países beneficiados con los préstamos son Argentina, Bolivia, Brasil, Chile, Ecuador, Honduras y Uruguay. "Estamos ampliando nuestro financiamiento y, al mismo tiempo, utilizando instrumentos que nos permiten movilizar más recursos, acompañar a gobiernos nacionales y locales y fortalecer al sector privado para acelerar el desarrollo de América Latina y el Caribe", dijo Sergio Díaz-Granados, presidente ejecutivo de CAF, citado en el comunicado.

item.title: ATP roundup: Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz advance in Asia
item.description: Alexander Zverev continued his stellar 2026 season, defeating Cameron Norrie of Great Britain 7-6 (1), 6-4 to advance at the China Open in Beijing on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Alexander Zverev continued his stellar 2026 season, defeating Cameron Norrie of Great Britain 7-6 (1), 6-4 to advance at the China Open in Beijing on Thursday. Winner of two Grand Slam tournaments this year, World No. 2 Zverev is moving closer to overtaking No. 1 Jannik Sinner of Italy. With the victory, the German also leads the ATP Tour with 28 hard-court wins on the year. In the Round of 16, the top-seeded Zverev will meet Juncheng Shang of China, the home favorite who defeated Argentine Sebastian Baez 5-7, 6-3, 7-5 Also moving on were fifth-seeded Alex de Minaur of Australia and Russian Roman Safiullin, who took out fourth-seeded Flavio Cobolli of Italy 6-3, 6-2. Alex Molcan of Slovakia, Francisco Cerundolo of Argentina, Quentin Halys of France, Russia's Andrey Rublev and Hubert Hurkacz of Poland also won. Japan Open Tennis Championships Top seed Carlos Alcaraz and second-seeded Frances Tiafoe advanced on a day that saw three of the top 10 seeds fall in Tokyo. Two Americans were among those sent home. Jaume Munar of Spain topped Taylor Fritz, the third seed, 6-7 (7), 6-4, 6-3. Ugo Humbert of France ousted fifth-seeded Brandon Nakashima 6-3, 6-2 and Italy's Luciano Darderi defeated Norway's Casper Ruud, the sixth seed, 7-6 (3), 6-3. Spain's Alcaraz advanced to the Round of 16 by staving off Alex Michelsen 7-6 (1), 4-6, 6-1. Tiafoe defeated Kei Nishikori of Japan 6-4, 6-4, sending Nishikori into his previously announced retirement with a loss in his home nation. Other winners were Jaime Faria of Portugal, Stefanos Tsitsipas of Greece, Kyrian Jacquet of France and Denis Shapovalov of Canada. --Field Level Media

item.title: US mortgage rates jump by most in 4 years in latest week
item.description: The interest rate on the most common US home loan shot up by a quarter percentage point this week to the highest in almost three years on the back of surging government bond yields, dealing another setback to would-be home buyers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The interest rate on the most common US home loan shot up by a quarter percentage point this week to the highest in almost three years on the back of surging government bond yields, dealing another setback to would-be home buyers. The rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage now averages 7.28%, up from 7.03% a week ago, Freddie Mac data showed on Thursday. It was the largest weekly increase in about four years. Mortgage rates are tied closely to the yield on US 10-year Treasury notes, which this week hit the highest in nearly a quarter century after data showed US economic growth was stronger in the first half of the year than previously estimated, momentum that is seen having continued through the third quarter. Furthermore, inflation remains elevated - more than 1 percentage point above the Federal Reserve's 2% target - and investors expect the Fed to respond with at least one more interest rate hike this year to lower inflation. The Freddie Mac data followed a similar reading of mortgage rates from the Mortgage Bankers Association, which on Wednesday also reported another drop in mortgage application volumes in the face of rising rates. The 30-year rate is up by more than 1.2 percentage points in the seven months since the US and Israel launched attacks against Iran, leading to a jump in global energy costs and feeding into a wider rise in inflation. "Mortgage rates increased for the sixth straight week, reaching a nearly three-year high," MBA President and CEO Bob Broeksmit said in a statement. "Affordability and borrower demand have weakened in recent weeks as the higher-rate environment continues to put pressure on both prospective homebuyers and homeowners looking to refinance.”

item.title: Airbus staff in Spain vote in favour of deal after weeks of strikes
item.description: Airbus staff in Spain voted to support a proposal to end months of stop-and-start strike action on Thursday, unions said in a statement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Airbus (AIR.PA) staff in Spain voted to support a proposal to end months of stop-and-start strike action on Thursday, unions said in a statement. The deal included recovering lost purchasing power on top of inflation-linked wage increases, flexibility in holidays and a return to 40% remote working, according to a document outlining the proposal seen by Reuters. A total of 87% of the workforce participated in the referendum on the preliminary deal reached with unions on September 4, according to the statement, with 20.26% voting against the proposal and 2.98% abstaining. Airbus declined to comment, saying it did not yet have official information. Strike action [USN:L8N43B1P5 TEXT:"began in July"] over issues including sub-inflation pay rises, tighter attendance monitoring and requirements for office staff to spend more time on site. An initial offer was rejected [USN:L8N44N0LB TEXT:"in late August"], prompting workers to resume their strike. Airbus, which employs around 14,500 workers in Spain, has eight sites in the country producing military transport planes and parts for commercial aircraft and satellites.

item.title: WBC heavyweight champion Kabayel's first defence confirmed for Duesseldorf on November 28
item.description: Germany's Agit Kabayel will make the first defence of his WBC world heavyweight belt against unbeaten Albanian Nelson Hysa in Duesseldorf on November 28, promoter Frank Warren confirmed on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany's Agit Kabayel will make the first defence of his WBC world heavyweight belt against unbeaten Albanian Nelson Hysa in Duesseldorf on November 28, promoter Frank Warren confirmed on Thursday. Kabayel, 34, was declared the WBC champion after Ukraine's Oleksandr Usyk [USN:L6N42Y12C TEXT:"relinquished the belt"] last June. Duesseldorf's 60,000 capacity Merkur Spiel Arena is close to Kabayel's hometown of Bochum but the fight will fall on Albanian independence day and Hysa, 42, can also count on strong support. "This is the fight we wanted to make," said Warren in a statement ahead of a launch event next week, with the fight due to be live on DAZN. "Agit Kabayel has rejuvenated the boxing market in Germany with his exploits in the heavyweight division and he will prove as much by defending his world title in front of over 60,000 fans in Duesseldorf on November 28." Both men are managed by Warren's Queensberry Promotions but Hysa does not feature in the latest WBC rankings, although he is fifth in the WBA's list of contenders.

item.title: Christa Pike está hospitalizada após sobreviver a execução no Tennessee
item.description: Christa Pike recebia cuidados médicos em um hospital de Nashville na quinta-feira, poucas horas depois de ter sobrevivido a duas tentativas do Tennessee de executá-la por meio de injeções letais, segundo seus advogados, o que reacendeu o debate sobre a pena de morte nos Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Allen
item.content:encoded: Christa Pike recebia cuidados médicos em um hospital de Nashville na quinta-feira, poucas horas depois de ter sobrevivido a duas tentativas do Tennessee de executá-la por meio de injeções letais, segundo seus advogados, o que reacendeu o debate sobre a pena de morte nos Estados Unidos. Pike, de 50 anos, foi condenada à morte na década de 1990 depois que um júri a considerou culpada por um homicídio que ela cometeu quando era adolescente. Sua execução mal sucedida na quarta-feira na Instituição de Segurança Máxima de Riverbend, a segunda neste ano no Tennessee, destaca as dificuldades que os Estados norte-americanos enfrentam para realizar injeções letais e encontrar métodos alternativos adequados para a pena capital. “Christa está viva neste momento”, disse Randall Spivey, um dos advogados de Pike, aos repórteres, na tarde de quinta-feira. “Não temos uma ideia de seu prognóstico nem muitas informações atualizadas sobre sua saúde no momento, mas sabemos que ela está viva agora e recebendo cuidados médicos que estão salvando sua vida.” O governador do Tennessee, Bill Lee, que na segunda-feira negou pedido de clemência de Pike para comutar sua pena para prisão perpétua, ordenou a suspensão das execuções programadas no Tennessee até o final do ano e uma análise independente da tentativa fracassada de quarta-feira. “Ninguém queria que o que aconteceu ontem à noite tivesse acontecido”, disse Lee, do Partido Republicano, aos repórteres. “É uma tragédia, e é profundamente perturbador para mim que isso tenha acontecido neste Estado. O povo merece melhor e vamos garantir que isso aconteça.” O Tennessee adotou, em 2024, um protocolo de injeção letal com um único medicamento, utilizando pentobarbital, um barbitúrico potente. Autoridades prisionais injetaram duas seringas em Pike, segundo informaram seus advogados em um documento judicial apresentado tarde da noite, causando-lhe “agonia desnecessária”, mas sem matá-la. Autoridades do Tennessee afirmaram que a execução foi interrompida e que ela foi levada em uma ambulância. Kayla Hackney, porta-voz do Departamento de Correções, se recusou a responder a perguntas sobre o estado de saúde de Pike na quinta-feira. Pike teria sido a primeira mulher executada pelo Tennessee em mais de dois séculos. A maioria dos países do mundo aboliu a pena de morte, e o alto comissário das Nações Unidas para os Direitos Humanos, Volker Turk, afirmou que o caso de Pike mostrou que os EUA deveriam seguir o exemplo. “O sofrimento prolongado – físico e mental – decorrente das múltiplas tentativas fracassadas de execução é repugnante e cruel”, disse Turk em comunicado. Pike tinha 18 anos em janeiro de 1995 quando ela, seu namorado de 17 anos, Tadaryl Shipp, e um terceiro companheiro atraíram Colleen Slemmer, uma colega de classe de 19 anos do centro profissionalizante Job Corps em Knoxville, para uma área arborizada, onde a torturaram e a mataram. Pike e Shipp confessaram o assassinato e ambos foram condenados por homicídio doloso qualificado.

item.title: California sets guardrails on lawyers' AI use
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed into law first-of-its-kind state legislation setting rules for how lawyers are permitted to use generative AI in their work.
item.dc:creator: Sara Merken
item.content:encoded: California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed into law first-of-its-kind state [USN:L6N44T194 TEXT:"legislation"] setting rules for how lawyers are permitted to use generative AI in their work. Newsom signed the bill, SB 574 , on Wednesday alongside a slate of other AI-related measures that he said are intended to protect workers, empower doctors and prevent fraudsters online. Courts across the country have imposed sanctions and issued warnings to lawyers who failed to vet AI-generated material and included “hallucinated” material in filings. Individual judges and courts have also issued standing orders setting guardrails on the use of AI. No other state has enacted a law targeted at lawyers' and arbitrators' use of the technology, though some attorneys have said the measure is partly duplicative of existing rules. The law builds on requirements that already bind lawyers under state rules governing civil litigation, such as the need for court filings to be supported by existing law. “The legislation overlaps with existing legal ethics rules but serves as a reminder that lawyers need to be checking and verifying the output received from AI tools,” Daren Orzechowski, a Silicon Valley-based M&A and technology transactions partner at A&O Shearman, said in an email. Under the new measure, an attorney cannot “delegate the practice of law” to generative AI. A lawyer responsible for submitting a filing in court must personally verify citations, including those provided by AI. Lawyers also must take “reasonable steps” to verify AI outputs, correct any false or hallucinated output in any AI-generated material they use, and disclose the use of AI for documents submitted in court. They are barred from entering confidential or other nonpublic information into certain generative AI systems. Arbitrators are restricted from delegating any decision-making to an AI tool. That new verification requirement likely won’t curb lawyers’ use of AI, but could “dramatically expand the amount of time that the signing attorney would be required to spend reviewing the legal and evidentiary citations in each filing,” said Ariel House, a litigation partner in Baker Botts' San Francisco office. Cite-checking court filings is frequently done by paralegals under a lawyer’s supervision, House said in an email. The requirement could be a heavy burden for solo practitioners and small law firms, while larger firms might be able to assign the task to a junior lawyer with a lower billing rate, she said. Jeff Fisher, a San Francisco-based trial lawyer at Farella Braun + Martel, said in an email that the California legislation underscores the need for lawyers to verify outputs and avoid entering confidential information in public generative AI systems. “That said, I do not see the law as a sea change in the way lawyers and law firms are continuing to expand their use of AI," Fisher wrote. "The benefits and efficiencies are too great to ignore.”

item.title: Ukraine's 2026 budget, defence needs are covered, EU says
item.description: The European Commission and Ukraine said on Thursday they had identified the funds to cover the country's budget and defence needs for 2026 and agreed to swiftly unlock more cash for 2027.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The European Commission and Ukraine said on Thursday they had identified the funds to cover the country's budget and defence needs for 2026 and agreed to swiftly unlock more cash for 2027. "We will also begin work on identifying additional budgetary and defence needs," the European Union's executive body and Ukraine said in a joint statement. As it continues to fight against Russia's 2022 invasion, Ukraine is relying heavily on payouts from a €90 billion loan from the EU for this year and next. Kyiv has been struggling to close a $27 billion funding gap to ensure it can still conduct combat operations at the start of 2027, Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi [USN:L1N45M0A3 TEXT:"said on Wednesday"]. But Thursday's joint statement said funds had been identified to cover spending for the remainder of this year - although it also alluded to the need for Ukraine to meet the EU's political reform benchmarks to access all the cash. "Today, through coordinated joint efforts, we have identified the means to cover Ukraine's budget and defence needs for 2026. We have also reconfirmed the steps needed to ensure their timely release," the statement said. Ukraine and the EU Commission also agreed to "move forward swiftly with the allocation of €45 billion" from the EU loan for 2027, "subject to the established conditions". Bloomberg reported earlier the EU had rejected a request from Ukraine to speed up loan payouts to cover its unexpected shortfall, citing people familiar with the matter. But an EU official familiar with the talks disputed that interpretation. "We have not closed any door," said the official, speaking on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential discussions. "Today we had a very productive meeting that ended with a clear path forward that ensures the necessary means for 2026 and start work together on 2027." A Commission spokesperson had no immediate comment and there was no immediate additional comment from Ukrainian officials. ($1 = 0.8911 euros)

item.title: EU wants coordinated approach with US on lowering diesel prices, Sefcovic says
item.description: European Union trade chief Maros Sefcovic said on Thursday that he discussed tight diesel supplies and price spikes with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and expressed Europe's desire for a coordinated approach to lowering prices.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder
item.content:encoded: European Union trade chief Maros Sefcovic said on Thursday that he discussed tight diesel supplies and price spikes with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and expressed Europe's desire for a coordinated approach to lowering prices. Sefcovic told reporters at the G20 trade ministers meeting that any move to restrict diesel exports would be unexpected and have detrimental effects on Europe's economic performance. [USN:L6N45N0FO TEXT:"Reuters reported earlier"] that the Trump administration has told France and Germany that they faced US diesel export restrictions if they failed to release the fuel from their strategic reserves. Sefcovic said he and Greer did not go into great detail on the topic, adding that Europe had exceeded its commitment to buy US energy under last year's trade agreement struck in Turnberry, Scotland. "We clearly decided to stay in close touch to avoid any surprises here," Sefcovic said of the diesel discussions. "And I understand that there is the intention and definitely strong preference from the European side for a coordinated approach and for finding the solutions, which I think would be first and foremost, secure the supply" for citizens on both sides of the Atlantic Ocean. "We have every interest in working together on lowering the prices, be it on diesel or also other products from oil and gas supplies," he added. Earlier, Greer told Bloomberg TV that he had [USN:L1N45N0PN TEXT:"discussed the diesel issue"] with European counterparts in Milwaukee and expressed the Trump administration's desire for them to release more diesel reserves.

item.title: Kashkari, de la Fed, prevé más alzas de tasas, pero no tiene claro si es necesario actuar este mes
item.description: El presidente de la Reserva Federal de Mineápolis, Neel Kashkari, dijo el jueves que prevé que serán necesarias nuevas alzas de tasas de interés para frenar la economía de cara a 2027, aunque no tiene claro si la próxima medida debería decidirse a finales de este mes.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: El presidente de la Reserva Federal de Mineápolis, Neel Kashkari, dijo el jueves que prevé que serán necesarias nuevas alzas de tasas de interés para frenar la economía de cara a 2027, aunque no tiene claro si la próxima medida debería decidirse a finales de este mes. "Tengo una actitud abierta" respecto a cómo procederá la Fed con las subidas de tasas de interés y "no tengo una opinión firme" sobre si la próxima subida debería darse en la reunión del 27 y 28 de octubre, dijo Kashkari a Reuters en una entrevista. La Fed celebrará su última reunión del año los días 8 y 9 de diciembre. Kashkari, que fue uno de los 12 responsables de política monetaria de la Fed que votaron el mes pasado a favor de elevar la tasa de referencia del banco central al rango entre 3,75% y 4,00%, señaló que sus previsiones presentadas para esa reunión apuntaban a un alza más de un cuarto de punto porcentual este año y otra en 2027. Y aunque se negó a calificar los riesgos en torno a sus perspectivas sobre las tasas de interés, señaló que sus previsiones ya se han visto cuestionadas. Desde la reunión de septiembre, "los datos que he obtenido sugieren que la economía está evolucionando incluso mejor de lo que había previsto" en un contexto en el que "la inflación sigue siendo demasiado alta", añadió Kashkari. "Si la economía demuestra ser increíblemente resistente y, por lo tanto, la inflación resulta ser probablemente más persistente de lo que creo, entonces podría ser necesario subir las tasas aún más de lo que preveo en este momento. Pero no sé" si así es como se desarrollarán los acontecimientos, dijo el presidente de la Fed de Mineápolis. CONTROL DE LA INFLACIÓN La Fed subió las tasas el mes pasado para frenar la alta inflación, que lleva más de media década superando el objetivo del 2% del banco central. Kashkari ya se había mostrado a favor de un aumento de las tasas de interés en la reunión de política monetaria de julio. Los responsables de la política monetaria, en la reunión del mes pasado, también previeron una subida más en 2026. Los mercados financieros esperaban que el endurecimiento monetario de la Fed fuera aún más agresivo hasta que el presidente de la Fed de Nueva York, John Williams, dijo el martes que, aunque considera probable otra alza este año, "no hay necesidad de urgencia". Los inversores redujeron drásticamente las probabilidades de una subida este mes tras las declaraciones de Williams. Aunque Kashkari señaló que la reciente alza de tasas de la Fed contribuyó a un fuerte aumento de los costos de financiación a largo plazo, dijo que la política monetaria no está contribuyendo mucho a frenar la economía. "El mercado laboral parece bastante sólido en estos momentos. Da la impresión de que la economía va bastante bien. Y cuando observo ese panorama, me digo: 'Vaya, probablemente la política monetaria no sea especialmente restrictiva en estos momentos'", agregó. Kashkari también señaló que los mercados están funcionando correctamente a pesar de la volatilidad actual. "No veo ningún indicio de riesgo sistémico" en los mercados, señaló. "Sí creo que hay que vigilar de cerca el sector bancario, y lo estamos haciendo", dado el rápido cambio en los costos de financiación. Kashkari señaló que el mercado de deuda pública parecía funcionar correctamente y ha sido capaz de asimilar los ajustes de precios.

item.title: Polish president says he signed windfall tax bill
item.description: Polish President Karol Nawrocki said on Thursday evening he signed a windfall tax bill which will be imposed on energy companies.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Polish President Karol Nawrocki said on Thursday evening he signed a windfall tax bill which will be imposed on energy companies. The Polish parliament approved the bill to tax windfall profits generated by oil and gas companies which have benefited from surging margins amid supply shocks due to the Middle East war. The bill assumes that 2026 revenues on sales of fuels exceeding the previous year average by 20% would be taxed at 60%. [USN:L8N4570B5 TEXT:"Prime Minister Donald Tusk"] said that if the bill becomes law, he would use proceeds to lower fuel prices at the pump. Nawrocki referred a previous version of the bill to the country's [USN:L8N43Q1C2 TEXT:"constitutional court"], pointing to concerns about its retroactive nature and potential effect on consumers.

item.title: Judge restores court-appointed top US prosecutor fired by Trump in Seattle
item.description: A federal judge ordered the Trump administration on Thursday to reinstate a court-appointed federal prosecutor in Seattle whom President Donald Trump fired less than an hour after his appointment.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella, Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A federal judge ordered the Trump administration on Thursday to reinstate a court-appointed federal prosecutor in Seattle whom President Donald Trump fired less than an hour after his appointment. Chief Judge Stanley Bastian of the federal court in Yakima, Washington,ruled preliminarily for Roger Rogoff in a [USN:L1N43H10H TEXT:"lawsuit he filed"] in July after his ouster as the court-appointed US attorney for the Western District of Washington. "Congress did not give the power to fill this inferior office to the president alone," Bastian said at the conclusion of a hearing on Thursday. The president, Bastian said, "cannot unilaterally fire a United States attorney appointed by the district court." The ruling marked the first legal victory for a court-appointed US attorney removed by the Trump administration amid a broader power struggle between the White House and the federal judiciary. The administration has ousted court-appointed US attorneys it did not favor in New York, New Jersey and Virginia, but Rogoff was the first to sue. The Justice Department has said Trump's firing of Rogoff was within the scope of executive power. Rogoff was [USN:L1N43H10H TEXT:"appointed"] by the judges of the Western District of Washington after the top post at the US attorney’s office had remained vacant without a Senate-confirmed nominee. Rogoff is an attorney at the law firm Osborn Machler & Neff. Bastian, an appointee of former President Barack Obama, said "Rogoff is the United States attorney for the Western District of Washington, and has been the rightful holder of that office since July 15, 2026, when he took the oath of office." The White House and Justice Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Trump recently nominated Pete Serrano to lead the office, which has 85 attorneys and 70 support staff. Bastian ordered the Trump administration to not obstruct Rogoff from accessing benefits and resources as the head of the US attorney's office.

item.title: What we know about the Cornell University rape investigation
item.description: New York state prosecutors have reopened an investigation into the alleged 2024 gang rape of a Cornell University student, after the woman filed a civil lawsuit last month saying several members of a campus fraternity drugged and assaulted her.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Ax
item.content:encoded: New York state prosecutors have reopened an investigation into the alleged 2024 gang rape of a Cornell University student, after the woman filed a civil lawsuit last month saying several members of a campus fraternity drugged and assaulted her. The case has prompted public outcry and raised questions about how law enforcement and the university initially responded after the woman, then 20, reported the incident to police a few weeks after it occurred. Here is what we know: WHAT DOES THE WOMAN SAY HAPPENED? The alleged victim, who uses the pseudonym Jane Doe in court papers, filed a lawsuit in New York in mid-September that named as defendants seven fraternity members, the Chi Phi fraternity, Cornell, a local bar and her own sorority. According to the lawsuit, she went to meet a friend at the Chi Phi fraternity house on October 19, 2024, after drinking earlier in the evening. The friend, a member of the fraternity, and other members plied her with alcohol, marijuana and ketamine, an anesthetic that can cause hallucinogenic effects, and sexually assaulted her after she became incapacitated, the lawsuit alleges. The complaint includes a screenshot of a group text chain among several fraternity members in which one man crudely encouraged others to join in the sexual activity. WHAT HAVE PROSECUTORS SAID? On Monday, the Tompkins County district attorney, Matthew Van Houten, said his office had reopened the case and would present evidence, including testimony from the woman, to a grand jury for possible indictment. Van Houten acknowledged the public outcry following the civil lawsuit and referred to "additional evidence," though he did not provide details. He offered a lengthy explanation for why prosecutors did not pursue criminal charges in 2024. The woman's sworn statement to police, he said, "described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious, and consensual." Prosecutors' decision was driven at least in part by New York's narrowly tailored sexual assault law. Under the law, it can be harder to bring rape charges in cases in which the victim willingly consumed alcohol or drugs. Several New York lawmakers this week renewed a years-long push to [USN:L1N45M14T TEXT:"rewrite state statutes"] to eliminate that distinction, arguing that it creates a potential loophole for rapists to avoid prosecution. Jane Doe's lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, has criticized prosecutors for not investigating further at the time and has told news outlets that the district attorney's office never spoke to his client before declining to bring charges. WHAT HAVE WE LEARNED ABOUT THE INITIAL INVESTIGATION? In recent days, several new reports have revealed more about what law enforcement knew in 2024. CBS New York obtained a copy of the transcript of Jane Doe's interview with police, which included far more detail than the sworn statement police eventually provided to prosecutors. "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped," she told police in mid-November, several weeks after the incident. That assertion was not included in the shorter written statement that Van Houten's office relied upon in deciding whether to pursue charges. The New York Times obtained more than 1,000 pages of material from Cornell's internal investigation into the incident. The documents show that the woman's understanding of the event shifted over time, the newspaper reported; she told police it took some time for her to fully realize that she had been gang-raped. WHAT HAS THE UNIVERSITY SAID? Cornell has defended its handling of the matter, saying that it launched a comprehensive investigation and barred from campus the Chi Phi chapter, which remains closed. The school imposed a range of discipline on the fraternity members, including expulsions and sanctions. The lawsuit claimed Cornell failed to adequately punish the alleged perpetrators and offered some a chance to mitigate their penalties by writing essays. On Wednesday, New York Governor Kathy Hochul said Cornell had agreed to hire an outside law firm to conduct a new investigation. WHAT HAS THE FRATERNITY SAID? The interim executive director of the national Chi Phi fraternity, Trey Robb, said in a statement on Wednesday that the Cornell chapter expelled members understood to have been involved in the incident, as did the national fraternity. "These actions went beyond anything the law or Cornell University required of us," Robb said. WHAT HAVE THE ACCUSED MEMBERS SAID? The New York Times, citing the internal Cornell documents, said the men all denied any wrongdoing and told school investigators that the sex was consensual. But in some comments, the men did express unease or concern about the interaction, the Times reported.

item.title: US states filed fraud lawsuit over Corteva's Vylor spinoff
item.description: A group of US states sued Corteva and Vylor on Thursday, alleging Corteva's spinoff of its seed business to Vylor was a fraudulent attempt to avoid tens of billions in legacy liabilities related to "forever chemicals" polluting the environment.
item.dc:creator: Dietrich Knauth
item.content:encoded: A group of US states sued Corteva (CTVA.N) and Vylor (VYLR.N) on Thursday, alleging Corteva's spinoff of its seed business to Vylor was a fraudulent attempt to avoid tens of billions in legacy liabilities related to "forever chemicals" polluting the environment. The lawsuit, filed in Indiana state court by 15 US states and the territory of Guam, alleges that Vylor received the "crown jewels" of Corteva's business without assuming its liabilities for perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). Corteva and Vylor are corporate successors to DuPont, which has been named in thousands of lawsuits alleging the company's chemicals have polluted the environment and exposed millions of Americans to potential health risks. Corteva completed the [USN:L3N3VI0R8 TEXT:"spinoff"] of its seed and genetics business into a separate publicly traded company on Thursday. Corteva was formed during the 2015 merger of Dow Chemical Company and DuPont, taking on the combined companies' agriculture business and becoming the corporate parent of the old DuPont companies, according to the complaint. At the time Corteva contractually assumed DuPont's PFAS liabilities, but the new Vylor transaction attempts to spin off the profitable seed business without taking on any of the old company's PFAS debts. The states allege that the spinoff is an attempt to defraud PFAS creditors by placing assets out of reach of their lawsuits against former DuPont companies.

item.title: Mattel attracts takeover interest from Authentic Brands Group, WSJ reports
item.description: Mattel has been approached by Authentic Brands Group for a takeover offer that could value the Barbie maker at around $6 billion or more, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mattel (MAT.O) has been approached by Authentic Brands Group for a takeover offer that could value the Barbie maker at around $6 billion or more, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. Authentic Brands was discussing a more than $20-a-share offer, according to the report. Shares of Mattel, which has a market capitalization of about $3.62 billion, were up 25% at $15.79 after the report. There is no guarantee that Mattel will be open to Authentic Brands' offer, and there is no formal sale process ongoing for the company, the report said. Mattel declined to comment, while Authentic Brands did not immediately respond to a Reuters request. Mattel shares closed down about 4% on Wednesday, after the company said its top boss Ynon Kreiz would leave to take on the role of co-CEO at Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) and run its combined business with Warner Bros (WBD.O) . At Mattel, Kreiz will be succeeded by Roger Lynch, the former CEO of the New Yorker-owner Conde Nast, on or before November 2026. Lynch's transition could complicate any deal for Mattel as he works on his strategy, the WSJ report said. Consumer goods companies and retailers are battling weak spending as households face higher fuel costs and interest rates in the US. This year, Mattel has struggled with tariff-related costs, even as it continued its push to build an entertainment portfolio around its brands, following the success of the 2023 "Barbie" movie. Its shares have dropped 33% so far this year. In May, Mattel investor Southeastern Asset Management called on Kreiz to [USN:L4N41L0QB TEXT:"explore options"] for the company, including going private, or being acquired by rival Hasbro (HAS.O) or a large media company that would value Mattel's IP assets better than the public market. Authentic Brands bought Dockers from Levi Strauss (LEVI.N) earlier this year, adding to its portfolio that includes Guess and Van Heusen. The company licenses intellectual property of its brands to partners, and has been focusing its M&A strategy to include kids entertainment brands and hospitality.

item.title: Serviço Postal dos EUA tomará medidas adicionais para garantir entrega das cédulas eleitorais
item.description: O Serviço Postal dos Estados Unidos (USPS) anunciou nesta quinta-feira que tomará uma série de medidas extraordinárias para garantir a entrega de milhões de cédulas eleitorais para as eleições legislativas de meio de mandato de 2026, que ocorrerão no próximo mês, incluindo a ampliação do horário de atendimento em algumas agências.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson, Jacob Bogage
item.content:encoded: O Serviço Postal dos Estados Unidos (USPS) anunciou nesta quinta-feira que tomará uma série de medidas extraordinárias para garantir a entrega de milhões de cédulas eleitorais para as eleições legislativas de meio de mandato de 2026, que ocorrerão no próximo mês, incluindo a ampliação do horário de atendimento em algumas agências. O USPS informou, em um memorando ao qual a Reuters teve acesso, que as agências podem estender o horário de atendimento a partir de 4 de outubro até a eleição de 3 de novembro para lidar com as cédulas eleitorais e estabelecer uma fila exclusiva para “Carimbo Postal de Cédulas Eleitorais” nos balcões ou uma opção de entrega de cédulas por drive-through. O USPS também realizará processamento acelerado, entregas extras, e coletas especiais de cédulas eleitorais. O USPS também informou que, antes da eleição, os funcionários poderão usar a rede Priority Mail Express para agilizar a entrega de cédulas preenchidas devolvidas pelos eleitores que, de outra forma, poderiam não ser entregues a tempo. A partir de 24 de outubro até o dia da eleição, os carteiros deverão verificar todos os pontos de entrega em busca de correspondência a ser enviada, independentemente de haver correspondência recebida. Em 14 de setembro, a Suprema Corte dos EUA se recusou a permitir que o USPS aplicasse uma regra voltada para cédulas eleitorais enviadas pelo correio, representando um revés para os esforços do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, de restringir o voto por correspondência. A agência adotou a medida depois que Trump emitiu, em março, um decreto com o objetivo de tornar mais rígidas as regras que regem o voto por correspondência. Em 2024, o USPS entregou 99,2 milhões de cédulas de eleitores na eleição presidencial. Cerca de 30% dos votos foram dados pelo correio na eleição presidencial de novembro de 2024, uma queda em relação aos 46% registrados em 2020. Os pares republicanos de Trump estão em uma disputa acirrada para manter o controle do Congresso nas eleições de meio de mandato. Restringir as cédulas eleitorais pelo correio beneficiaria os republicanos, já que os eleitores democratas utilizam desproporcionalmente esse método, de acordo com várias pesquisas. De acordo com a regra que foi bloqueada, os Estados teriam que fornecer listas de destinatários de cédulas por correspondência ao USPS e utilizar envelopes de envio e devolução aprovados pela agência, equipados com códigos de barras exclusivos. O Serviço Postal poderia então se recusar a enviar cédulas que não estivessem em conformidade ou que estivessem associadas a eleitores que não constassem nas listas. (Reportagem de David Shepardson e Jacob Bogage)

item.title: Messi se convierte en el accionista mayoritario del club español Eldense
item.description: El futbolista argentino Lionel Messi completó la adquisición del CD Eldense, un equipo de la Segunda División española, a la espera de la aprobación de las autoridades reguladoras, anunció el club este jueves.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El futbolista argentino Lionel Messi completó la adquisición del CD Eldense, un equipo de la Segunda División española, a la espera de la aprobación de las autoridades reguladoras, anunció el club este jueves. Messi, de 39 años, se ha convertido así en el propietario mayoritario de un segundo club en España este año, tras la compra de la UE Cornellá en abril. El exdelantero de la selección argentina y del Barcelona, que actualmente juega en el Inter de Miami, acordó el mes pasado la compra de todas las acciones del Eldense que estaban en manos de un grupo inversor colombiano, el anterior accionista mayoritario. "El Club Deportivo Eldense anuncia oficialmente la adquisición del club por parte de Leo Messi, lo que marca el inicio de un nuevo y emocionante capítulo en la historia del club, que se remonta a más de cien años", escribió el Eldense, fundado en 1921, en la página web del club. El Eldense espera que este acuerdo le dé un impulso. El club está en el puesto 19º de la Segunda División, con cuatro derrotas en siete partidos, y lucha por evitar el descenso.

item.title: Trump moves swiftly to fill seat on conservative-packed US appeals court
item.description: US President Donald Trump moved swiftly on Thursday to fill a newly-opened seat on a conservative-leaning federal appeals court, announcing he would nominate a Mississippi lawyer to succeed a judge for whom the lawyer had served as a law clerk.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump moved swiftly on Thursday to fill a newly-opened seat on a conservative-leaning federal appeals court, announcing he would nominate a Mississippi lawyer to succeed a judge for whom the lawyer had served as a law clerk. Trump in a social media post said he is nominating Todd Butler, a partner at law firm Phelps Dunbar, to serve on the New Orleans-based 5th US Circuit Court of Appeals. Butler would succeed US Circuit Judge Leslie Southwick, who on Monday [USN:L1N45K0Q2 TEXT:"announced plans"] to retire from active service on the federal bench. It was one of three judicial nominations that the president announced on Thursday. The Republican-led US Senate recessed on Wednesday until after the November 3 midterm elections, in which Democrats hope to reclaim control of the chamber. This means that Butler's nomination and Trump's two new picks to serve as judges in federal district courts in North Carolina will not be considered by the Senate until its lame-duck session. The 5th Circuit hears appeals of cases arising out of Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas. Twelve of its 17 judges were appointed by Republican presidents, including Southwick, [USN:N24528852 TEXT:"who was appointed"] by Republican President George W. Bush. The court has become a [USN:L1N41O0SM TEXT:"favored destination"] for conservatives, including activists and Republican state attorneys general, challenging federal regulations, abortion policies and gun control measures. Trump appointed six of the 5th Circuit's judges in his first term, and in June announced the [USN:L1N432037 TEXT:"nomination"] of US District Judge Anna St. John, a former conservative legal activist who had only recently been confirmed to the US District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana, to succeed another judge taking senior status. In nominating Butler to succeed Southwick, Trump noted that he had previously clerked for the judge and had the backing of both of Mississippi's Republican senators. He called Butler "a strong defender of Law Enforcement throughout his career." Butler last year argued before the US Supreme Court as counsel to the city of Brandon, Mississippi, in a lawsuit by a street preacher who said his religious rights were violated when he was convicted of violating a local ordinance. The US Supreme Court in March issued a unanimous decision in that case, Olivier v. City of Brandon, Mississippi, and ruled for the preacher, allowing him to pursue his lawsuit. The two new North Carolina judge nominees are Philip Aubart, a top prosecutor in the US Attorney's Office in the Eastern District of North Carolina, who was nominated to serve as a judge in the state's Middle District, and US Magistrate Judge Brian Meyers, who Trump wants to elevate to a district court judge position in the Eastern District. Read more: [USN:L1N45K0Q2 TEXT:"Trump gains second vacancy to fill on appeals court dominated by conservatives"] [USN:L1N41O0SM TEXT:"In the US South, an appeals court leans farther right than the Supreme Court"]

item.title: Vídeo não mostra manifestantes jogando ovos em carro de Janja; imagens são da Albânia
item.description: Um vídeo em que manifestantes jogam ovos em um carro mostra um protesto na Albânia em julho deste ano, e não um ataque contra um veículo com a primeira-dama Janja Lula da Silva, como afirmam publicações no Facebook.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo em que manifestantes jogam ovos em um carro mostra um protesto na Albânia em julho deste ano, e não um ataque contra um veículo com a primeira-dama Janja Lula da Silva, como afirmam publicações no Facebook. Aqui estão os principais detalhes: “Janja tem carro atingido por ovos durante passagem por Brasília”, diz o enunciado que acompanha o vídeo. A legenda afirma que a manifestação aconteceu no dia 27, próximo a um ato político do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. O vídeo, porém, circula nas redes sociais desde o final de julho. O canal de TV Al Arabiya publicou uma versão mais longa da gravação no dia 24 daquele mês. Segundo a emissora, as imagens mostram um protesto em Tirana, capital da Albânia, contra a construção de um resort de luxo . A Reuters confirmou pelo Google Street View que as imagens foram feitas em Tirana -- o mesmo prédio aparece nos registros da ferramenta e no vídeo checado. Uma notícia do Metrópoles e uma publicação de Janja no Instagram mostram que ela esteve no Distrito Federal na data mencionada nos posts, onde acompanhou uma carreata do candidato a governador Leandro Grass (PT). O carro da primeira-dama de fato foi atingido por ovos durante o evento, segundo noticiado pela TMC . A Reuters já verificou o mesmo vídeo sendo atribuído a um protesto contra Lula. Veredicto: Legenda errada. O protesto mostrado no vídeo ocorreu na Albânia, e não durante a participação de Janja em uma carreata em Brasília. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 .
